Before You Begin

The Legacy Wedding Blueprint

Most couples start wedding planning with a venue search and a spreadsheet. The Blueprint starts somewhere better: with the two of you. A free three-part assessment that uncovers your family heritage, puts words to your shared values, and turns both into decisions you can stand behind together.

Free Three parts, taken at your pace Answer together or invite your fiancé
Start Your Legacy Blueprint

A Note From Jessica

Why I Built This

I created the Blueprint because I believe lasting marriages are built on strong foundations, and planning a wedding is the first real test of that foundation. Most couples start with a checklist and a venue tour. The questions that shape the day, what you value, how you decide, whose voices count, usually get asked only after something goes sideways.

The Blueprint asks them first. It gathers the conversations worth having before the planning begins into one guided experience you complete as a couple. Your answers become the foundation for every choice that follows, whether you plan with us or on your own.

What’s Inside

Three Parts, One Foundation

Part One

Understanding Your Foundation

Begin with the families that shaped you. Favorite traditions, food and holiday memories, the values you each want to carry into your marriage, and what money well spent means to both of you.

  • Family heritage discovery
  • A 20-point values exercise that asks you to choose
  • Your wedding vision statement
Part Two

Partnership Planning Assessment

Discover how the two of you actually work together. Planning temperaments, love languages, and where your decision-making styles align or pull in different directions.

  • Your planning personality types
  • Compatibility across decisions, family, and budget
  • Wedding elements matched to how you love
Part Three

The Wedding Planning Toolkit

Turn understanding into strategy. Decide who gets a say, rank what matters in a vendor, and get an honest read on how much planning support fits your life right now.

  • Family input boundaries, set kindly
  • Vendor evaluation priorities
  • Your personalized planning report

How It Works

Made For Two

1

Start together

Create your Blueprint and invite your fiancé by email. Each of you answers from any device, on your own time.

2

Answer honestly

Your progress saves automatically. Pause after any question and pick up where you left off next week if you need to.

3

See yourselves clearly

Your results show where you align, where you differ, and what that means for planning. Download the full report or talk it through with us.

Common Questions

Before You Ask

What is the Legacy Wedding Blueprint?
A free three-part assessment for engaged couples, created by destination wedding planner Jessica Lueken of Aisle to Islands. It walks you through your family heritage, your shared values, how you work together as a couple, and the planning decisions worth settling before you book a single vendor.
Is it free?
Yes. The full three-part Blueprint is free, and your results are yours to keep whether or not you ever work with us.
How long does it take?
About an hour across all three parts, and you do not need to do it in one sitting. Your progress saves automatically after every question, so you can pause anywhere and return on any device.
Do both of us have to answer?
The Blueprint is built for two. You can answer side by side, or invite your fiancé by email and each complete your questions separately. Your results compare both sets of answers to show where you align and where a conversation is worth having.
What do we get when we finish?
A personalized report covering your values and how they align, your planning temperaments, your wedding vision statement, and a recommendation for how much planning support fits your situation. It is a starting foundation for your planning, not a finished wedding plan.

Before the Venue, Before the Dress

Build the Foundation First

The Blueprint is free, it is yours to keep, and it makes every conversation that follows easier, including the ones with us.
